h1: The 6 Best Heavy-Duty Electric Pruning Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Electric Pruning Shears: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six heavy-duty cordless electric pruning shears, from 1.65 to 2.75 inch cutting diameters, with battery and motor details.
summary: The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch model is the pick for the thickest branches, with two batteries and spare blades. The ANTTCTIG 2.56 inch version trims the price, and the SEESII 2.2 inch adds four modes for varied work. The 2.1 inch SK7-blade model is the one that names its steel, and the KOMOK suits all-day orchard jobs.
intro: Electric pruning shears are sold on a single big number, the cutting diameter, and buyers often pay for capacity they never use. A 2.75 inch cut matters on old orchard limbs, but for most shrubs and fruit trees a smaller head is lighter and faster.

We reviewed six cordless models and ranked them on paper by cutting diameter, motor type, battery setup, blade details and control modes. Cutting diameters and battery specs come from the listings. Prices are bucketed.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.75'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: The largest cutting capacity in this group, with a full kit.
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch model cuts branches up to 2.75 inches and ships with two batteries and spare blades. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

The 2.75 inch ANTTCTIG wins out as the capacity is the widest here and the spare blades keep it running when an edge dulls. The 2.56 inch sibling is almost as capable but a bit smaller.

Choose it for thick orchard limbs. The caveat is that a bigger head means more weight in the hand.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.56'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: Nearly the same kit with a slightly smaller cut.
products.description:
This ANTTCTIG cuts up to 2.56 inches and includes two batteries and spare blades, in the $50-100 bucket.

The 2.56 inch ANTTCTIG follows as the difference from the 2.75 inch model is only about 0.2 inches, which most gardeners never notice. It gives up that margin for a model that might be priced lower.

Best for general heavy pruning. If you routinely hit the largest limbs, step up to the 2.75.
products.skipIf: You need the very largest cut.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 2.2" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: Four modes for matching cut speed to branch thickness.
products.description:
The SEESII has a 2.2 inch cutting diameter, a brushless motor and four modes, in the $100-200 bucket.

The SEESII takes bronze as its modes help on varied work but it costs more than the ANTTCTIG pair, and the listing does not mention batteries. Compared with its 1.8 inch sibling it handles thicker wood.

It suits mixed pruning of shrubs and fruit trees. Check the product page for the battery setup.

products.name: 2.1"/54mm Electric Pruning Shears, Upgraded Cordless Electric Scissors, Brushless Motor, Dual 2.0Ah Battery, Sk7 Blade, LCD Display for Heavy-Duty Garden, Orchard & Branch Cutter
products.verdict: The only one here that names its blade steel.
products.description:
This 2.1 inch (54mm) model has a brushless motor, an SK7 blade, an LCD display and dual 2.0Ah batteries, in the $50-100 bucket.

The SK7 model holds fourth as naming the SK7 steel adds some assurance on edge durability, but 2.1 inches is smaller than the ANTTCTIG models and the brand is unlisted.

It suits orchard owners who like a battery readout. Expect a smaller cut than the top two.

products.name: Electric Pruning Shears, Upgraded 2.1" Cutting Garden Shears with LCD Display, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: A 2.1 inch brushless kit with an LCD and two batteries.
products.description:
This model offers a 2.1 inch cutting diameter, a brushless motor, an LCD display and two 2Ah batteries, in the $50-100 bucket.

The LCD brushless set lands fifth as it matches the specs of the SK7 model above but does not name its blade steel. Brushless motors generally run cooler and last longer than brushed ones.

Choose it for backyard fruit trees and hedges. Buy it only if the price is below the SK7 version.

products.name: KOMOK Electric Pruning Shears, Professional Cordless Electric Pruners Battery Powered Tree Branch Cutter, 1.65" (42mm) Cutting Diameter
products.verdict: Smaller cut, but a stated 8 to 10 hour runtime.
products.description:
The KOMOK has a 1.65 inch (42mm) cutting diameter, two 2Ah batteries and a listed 8 to 10 hour runtime, in the $100-200 bucket.

The KOMOK brings up the rear as the cutting capacity is the smallest here and it costs more than the ANTTCTIG pair. The runtime claim is the draw, so treat it as the maker's number.

Best for long vineyard or orchard days with lighter wood.

whatMatters.detail: This is the thickest branch the blade can cut, as rated by the maker. Running at the limit strains the motor. Pick a model with 0.5 inch spare over your usual branch size.
Brushless motors have no carbon brushes to wear out, so they tend to run cooler and last longer. Look for the word brushless in the title.
A 2Ah battery stores less than a 4Ah one, so runtime is shorter. Two batteries let you swap mid-job. Check the Ah and count.
Spare blades extend a kit's life. A named steel such as SK7 hints at hardness. Look for spares and the steel name in the listing.
Modes let you change cut speed, and an LCD shows battery. Both are conveniences, not necessities. Check which you actually want.

howToChoose.intro: Match the cut to your wood.

cards.label: Bigger head
cards.text: Cuts thicker limbs but tires your hand. Picks: ANTTCTIG 2.75'' and 2.56''.

cards.label: Smaller head
cards.text: Lighter for long days. Picks: KOMOK 1.65" and the 2.1" models.

howToChoose.note: Most home orchard owners should default to a 2.1 to 2.5 inch cut.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Two batteries, a cutting diameter above 2 inches and spare blades.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The ANTTCTIG 2.75'' and 2.56'' both include two batteries and spare blades.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want multiple modes or a longer runtime. The SEESII 2.2" or KOMOK fit.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a few trees. The ANTTCTIG 2.56'' is enough.

faq.q: Are electric pruners safe for beginners?
faq.a: Yes with care. Keep fingers clear of the blade and remove the battery when changing blades.
Cutting branches near the maximum diameter all day. That overheats the motor.
Generally yes for frequent use because there are no brushes to wear. For occasional use it matters less.

faq.q: How do I set up the battery?
faq.a: Charge fully before first use and lock the battery into the handle.

faq.q: How do I maintain the blades?
faq.a: Clean sap after use and apply a light oil to the blade.
They can cut up to their rated diameter, but dry hard wood is tougher. Stay below the limit.

finalTake: The ANTTCTIG 2.75'' kit is the best heavy-duty pick for thick limbs, and the 2.56'' version is the value alternative. The SEESII suits mixed work. Buy by branch size, not by the biggest number.
